To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concept of the time-dependent instantaneously occupied phase-space volume allows for a) the investigation of entropy flow between components of multi-component systems, b) the evaluation of the partial entropies of the components of multi-component system, and c) the derivation of the information flow between observer and observed system, and that this is the basis for a) the resolution of the paradoxical situation created by Jaynes' concept of an anthropomorphic entropy and b) the derivation of an intrinsic observer.

the entropy flow is a consequence of the observer's choice of a subsystem, the partial entropies of the subsystems are not conserved, the entropy flow is related to the intake of work, the intake of work and entropy flow can be linked to a cognitive situation and that the Gödelian nature of the cognitive process is an intrinsic feature of thermodynamics.
the entropy flow between parts of multi-component systems can be evaluated in a consistent way and is related to an observational situation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and in which way a physical theory can be formulated which is able to describe and explain the world as we experience it.
the question of how to describe the physical world in a more adequate way.
the following questions: What is a thermodynamic system, what are the components of a system?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entropy flow and the information flow are two sides of the same coin.
the physical world is not only Gödelian but also anthropomorphic in a most serious sense.
the physical world is not only observer-dependent but also observer-dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entropy of a system is a property of the system and not of the system plus observer.
the thermodynamic entropy of a system is the information about the system that is not accessible to a particular observer.
it is the first time that the entropy concept is applied to a situation in which a physical observer is involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of an observer is not only a necessary but also a natural consequence of thermodynamics.
the entropy flow and the partial entropies are not only a matter of the system but are also related to the observer and the observations.
the concept of entropy is not a property of the physical world but rather an attribute of an observer who is able to assign an entropy number to an observed situation.
